items.new: In connection with the monstrous pictures of whales, I am strongly tempted here to take up those still more monstrous stories about them which are found in certain books, both ancient and modern, especially in Pliny, Purchas, Hackluyt, Harris, Cuvier, and so forth. But I will let that matter pass.

items.new: Of the Right Whale, the best outline pictures are in Scoresby. But they are drawn on too small a scale to give the impression one would want. He has only one picture of whaling scenes, and this is a sad deficiency, because it is only through such pictures, when done well, that you can get anything like a truthful idea of the living whale as seen by his living hunters.

items.new: In the second engraving, the boat is in the act of drawing alongside the barnacled flank of a large running Right Whale, which rolls his black weedy bulk in the sea like some mossy rock-slide from the Patagonian cliffs. His jets are upright, full, and black like soot, so that from so abundant a smoke in the chimney, you would think there must be a fine supper cooking in the great bowels below. Sea birds are pecking at the small crabs, shellfish, and other sea candies and macaroni which the Right Whale sometimes carries on his pestilent back. And all the while the thick-lipped leviathan is rushing through the deep, leaving tons of tumultuous white curds in his wake, and causing the light boat to rock in the swells like a skiff caught near the paddle-wheels of an ocean steamer. Thus the foreground is all raging commotion; but behind, in admirable artistic contrast, is the glassy level of a becalmed sea, the drooping, unstarched sails of the powerless ship, and the inert mass of a dead whale, a conquered fortress, with the flag of capture hanging lazily from the whale-pole stuck into his spout-hole.

With the same marvelous patience, and with the same single shark's tooth of his one poor jackknife, he will carve you a bit of bone sculpture — not quite as expertly made, but as densely packed in its maze-like design as the Greek savage Achilles's shield, and full of barbaric spirit and suggestion, as the prints of that fine old Dutch savage, Albert Durer.

items.new: At some old gable-roofed country houses you will see brass whales hung by the tail as knockers on the roadside door. When the porter is sleepy, the anvil-headed whale would work best. But these knocking whales are seldom noteworthy as faithful likenesses. On the steeples of some old-fashioned churches you will see sheet-iron whales placed there as weather-vanes. But they are so high up, and besides are to all intents and purposes labeled "Hands off!" — so you cannot examine them closely enough to judge their merit.

items.new: But one transparent blue morning, when a stillness almost supernatural spread over the sea — though with no stagnant calm about it — when the long burnished path of sunlight on the waters seemed a golden finger laid across them, commanding some secrecy, when the slippered waves whispered together as they softly ran on — in this profound hush of the visible world, a strange apparition was seen by Daggoo from the main-masthead.

items.new: Whether the fleeting attendance of that one still and solitary jet had gradually worked upon Ahab, so that he was now prepared to connect the ideas of gentleness and calm with the first sight of the particular whale he hunted — however this was, or whether his eagerness misled him — whichever way it might have been, no sooner did he clearly perceive the white mass than with fierce intensity he instantly gave orders for lowering.

items.new: In recent years, Manilla rope has in the American fishery almost entirely replaced hemp as a material for whale-lines. Though not as durable as hemp, it is stronger and far more soft and elastic. And I will add — since there is an aesthetics in all things — it is much more handsome and becoming to the boat than hemp. Hemp is a dusky, dark fellow, a sort of Indian; but Manilla is like a golden-haired Circassian to look at.
